description: Problems people hit on Next.js, React, Vite and React Native stacks that denext handles, each backed by a named test in this repository. Source of truth for https://denext.dev/docs/fixed (generated by `deno task docs:fixed`); tests/catalog-fixed.test.ts fails when an evidence test disappears or is renamed.

kinds.fix: denext does not have the problem.
kinds.difference: denext behaves differently on purpose; read the entry before relying on it.
kinds.tradeoff: denext accepts the code instead of failing, at a cost the entry names.
kinds.capability: Something the other stack needs a separate service, plugin or package for, built into denext.

entries.title: One codebase for web, iOS, Android and desktop
entries.problem: Shipping the same React app to the web, the app stores and the desktop usually means separate projects (a web framework, a React Native app, an Electron app) with code shared through packages.
entries.cause: Each target has its own toolchain and module resolution, so per-platform code ends up in per-platform projects.
entries.denext: One denext app builds for every target. A module can have per-platform variants (`button.ios.tsx`, `button.web.tsx`, `button.desktop.tsx`) and the build for each target picks its variant; a module with no file for the target fails the build and names the variants it found.

evidence.name: staticExport: a module with no file for the target fails naming its variants
denext build + start: the web target's `.web` variant reaches the bundle and the render

entries.title: A Vite React SPA as a desktop app, without Electron
entries.problem: Turning an existing Vite React app into a desktop app usually means adding Electron or Tauri and a second build.
entries.cause: A browser SPA has no native window or packaging of its own.
entries.denext: `denext migrate --desktop` keeps the app's source, writes a denext config in SPA mode and a `desktop.ts` entry, and the app runs in a native window through Deno Desktop. An optional backend is reached through a same-origin proxy.

evidence.name: migrate SPA (pnpm + --desktop): config, aliases, env union, tailwind, parsed proxy

entries.title: Desktop apps without full system privileges
entries.problem: An Electron app's main process runs with full Node.js privileges, so every dependency it loads can read and write anywhere the user can.
entries.cause: Node.js has no permission model on by default, and the Electron main process is a Node.js process.
entries.denext: A packaged denext desktop app runs under Deno's permission model. The packaging scripts derive the `--allow-*` flags from the capabilities the app declares (`desktop.capabilities`) instead of granting everything; with no capabilities the app gets loopback network, read and env only.

evidence.name: desktopBuildFlags: no capabilities → only the loopback + read + env baseline (never -A)
desktopBuildFlags: the full capability set on Windows, least-privilege

entries.title: iOS momentum scrolling stops when a virtual list corrects its scroll position
entries.problem: In iOS Safari and WKWebView, a fling on a virtualized list stops dead or jumps when the list adjusts `scrollTop` while the momentum scroll is still running (for example after measuring rows).

affects.stack: React virtual lists on iOS WebKit

entries.cause: WebKit on iOS cancels the native momentum animation when script writes the scroll position during it.
entries.denext: denext defers scroll writes made during a touch or momentum phase: the content is shifted visually and the accumulated correction is applied in one step when the scroll ends. It is installed automatically for iOS WebKit visitors (`momentumSafeScroll: false` opts out).

evidence.name: momentum scroll: during momentum a scrollTop assignment is deferred
momentum scroll: corrections accumulate, and read-then-correct converges

entries.title: Inverted FlatList on the web scrolls the wrong way
entries.problem: With react-native-web, an `inverted` FlatList (the usual chat layout) scrolls in the opposite direction to the mouse wheel and reverses text selection.
entries.cause: react-native-web implements `inverted` with a `scaleY(-1)` transform, which flips the scroll and selection direction along with the layout.
entries.denext: In React Native mode, FlatList runs on denext's VirtualList and `inverted` is a logical reversal: item 0 is at the bottom without a transform, `onEndReached` fires at the visual top, and `scrollToIndex` / `scrollToOffset` are mirrored.

evidence.name: FlatList inverted: a logical reversal — item 0 at the bottom, no scaleY, header at the bottom
FlatList inverted: chat semantics — onEndReached is the visual top; scrollToIndex / scrollToOffset mirror

entries.title: Reanimated on the web without the Babel plugin
entries.problem: Reanimated worklets fail on the web when the Babel plugin is missing from the web build, and the plugin ties the build to Babel.
entries.cause: Reanimated relies on a Babel plugin to capture each worklet's closure at build time.
entries.denext: denext's React Native mode captures worklet closures with its own transform during the build, so Reanimated runs on the web with no Babel plugin, and reports the call it cannot derive a closure for by file and line.

evidence.name: worklets: hook callbacks capture what the Babel plugin captures
reanimatedWorkletsPlugin: stamps gated modules, app and node_modules; warns at file:line

entries.title: Over-the-air UI updates without a hosted update service
entries.problem: Shipping a UI fix to a mobile app without a store review usually depends on a hosted update service.
entries.cause: The app binary bundles its UI, so a change needs a new binary unless something downloads and activates a new bundle.
entries.denext: A denext app in the Capacitor shell checks a manifest you host (`denext ota manifest`, optionally signed), downloads the changed files and applies them on the next start. A binary whose native layer does not match the manifest refuses the update.

evidence.name: checkForUiUpdate: a different version → apply with baseUrl, headers, manifest
ota manifest: any changed file changes the version
onNativeUpdateRequired: fired for native_too_old / native_mismatch only; a throw is swallowed

entries.title: Middleware bypass through x-middleware-subrequest (CVE-2025-29927)
entries.problem: A request carrying the `x-middleware-subrequest` header skips Next.js middleware, including auth checks done there.
entries.cause: Next.js used an internal header to stop middleware recursion and trusted it on incoming requests.
entries.denext: denext's middleware runner has no request header that skips it; the test sends the attack header and the middleware still runs. Internal `x-middleware-*` markers are also never copied onto a response.
entries.upstreamFirst: Upgrade Next.js to 15.2.3, 14.2.25, 13.5.9 or 12.3.5 (or later). That is the fix for a Next.js app; denext's behaviour is listed for teams evaluating it, not as a substitute for the upgrade.

evidence.name: CVE-2025-29927: x-middleware-subrequest cannot bypass auth middleware
internal-header: x-middleware-* markers never leak onto a response (CVE-2026-44572)

entries.title: Cache poisoning of rendered pages (CVE-2024-46982, CVE-2025-49826)
entries.problem: A crafted request could make Next.js cache the wrong response for a page: a data response stored as the HTML page, or a non-200 response cached for a route.
entries.cause: Variants of one route shared a cache entry, and some error responses were cacheable.
entries.denext: denext keys the soft-navigation data variant separately from the HTML document and never stores a non-200 render in the page cache.
entries.upstreamFirst: Upgrade Next.js to the patched release named in each advisory (GitHub Security Advisories for vercel/next.js). denext's behaviour is listed for teams evaluating it, not as a substitute for the upgrade.

evidence.name: CVE-2024-46982/32421: soft-nav data variant cannot poison the HTML cache
CVE-2025-49826: a non-200 (notFound) render is never cached

entries.title: Image optimizer abuse (CVE-2024-47831, CVE-2025-55173, CVE-2025-57752)
entries.problem: The image optimization endpoint could be pushed into denial of service, made to serve an attacker-controlled download, or forward user credentials to the image's origin.
entries.cause: The optimizer accepted unbounded variants, passed through upstream response headers, and reused request credentials for the upstream fetch.
entries.denext: denext's image endpoint bounds the width and quality to an allowlist, rejects decompression bombs, never emits `Content-Disposition` or HTML, never serves `image/svg+xml`, and forwards no user credentials upstream.
entries.upstreamFirst: Upgrade Next.js to the patched release named in each advisory (GitHub Security Advisories for vercel/next.js). denext's behaviour is listed for teams evaluating it, not as a substitute for the upgrade.

evidence.name: CVE-2024-47831/44577: the image endpoint bounds width + rejects a bomb
CVE-2025-55173: image endpoint never emits an attacker download (no Content-Disposition, no html)
CVE-2025-57752: the image optimizer forwards no user credentials upstream

entries.title: Server Components payload deserialization (CVE-2025-55182, CVE-2025-55184)
entries.problem: A crafted request to a Server Function endpoint could run code on the server or hang it while the React Server Components payload was decoded.

affects.stack: React Server Components in Next.js App Router

entries.cause: The payload decoder reconstructed server references and nested structures from client input.
entries.denext: denext decodes a Server Action body with plain `JSON.parse`: a payload shaped like a server reference stays inert data, deep nesting is bounded, `__proto__` keys do not pollute prototypes, and an oversized body is refused before the handler runs.
entries.upstreamFirst: Upgrade React and Next.js to the patched releases named in the advisories. denext's behaviour is listed for teams evaluating it, not as a substitute for the upgrade.

evidence.name: RSC-RCE: a payload shaped like a server reference is decoded as inert data, never invoked
RSC-DoS: a deeply nested payload is bounded (JSON.parse throws, caught) — no hang

entries.title: Server-only code bundled for the browser
entries.problem: A client bundle pulls in a module that uses `fs`, a database driver or secrets. The build fails with an unhelpful resolution error, or worse, the code ships.
entries.cause: Anything a client component imports, directly or through a shared helper, goes into the client bundle; nothing flags server-only modules unless they import the `server-only` package.
entries.denext: The build fails with `denext: server-only code would ship to the browser`, naming the module, why it is server-only (a `node:` import, the `Deno` global) and the route that shipped it, and suggests the fix. No marker import is needed.

evidence.name: build fails when a hydrating route's tree would ship node:sqlite + Deno.env to the browser
checkEnvPoison: server-only in a client bundle is a build error

entries.title: Event handlers passed from a Server Component
entries.problem: Passing `onClick` or another function from a Server Component to a Client Component fails at render time.
errorText: Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props.
entries.cause: Props crossing the server/client boundary are serialized, and a function cannot be serialized unless it is a Server Action.
entries.denext: denext drops the function prop and prints one development warning per component and prop that names both fixes (make it a Server Action, or move the handler into a `"use client"` component). The `denext/no-handlers-in-async` lint rule reports it before the code runs. The handler still does not run, so treat the warning as an error.

evidence.name: a function prop from a Server Component to a client component warns once in dev
flags an inline arrow / function handler in an async component

entries.title: A page that uses hooks without "use client"
entries.problem: A page or layout that calls `useState` or another hook fails because it is a Server Component by default.
errorText: You're importing a component that needs useState
It only works in a Client Component but none of its parents are marked with "use client"
entries.cause: Server Components cannot hold state or effects, and a module is a Server Component unless it or an importer says `"use client"`.
entries.denext: denext hydrates the route instead of failing: the page renders on the server and becomes interactive in the browser. The cost is a larger client bundle for that route, and the build still fails if the route reaches a server-only module. Keeping hooks in a `"use client"` file remains the better shape.

evidence.name: interactive: hooks, event handlers, and dynamic() each force hydration

entries.title: A strict Content Security Policy without nonces or dynamic rendering
entries.problem: Adding a strict CSP to a Next.js app means generating a nonce in middleware, which makes every page dynamically rendered.
entries.cause: A nonce must be unique per response, so pages that carry one cannot be statically generated or cached.
entries.denext: Every denext page response carries a strict CSP by default. It is hash-based (the framework's own inline code is hashed), so static, cached, streamed and partially prerendered pages keep it. Routes opt external hosts in per directive, or opt out.

evidence.name: a page response carries a strict default CSP
a cache hit reuses the stored CSP
computeStreamingCsp: script-src carries the swap runtime hash

entries.title: "process is not defined" in the browser
entries.problem: An npm library or app module reads `process.env` in code that runs in the browser and throws on load.
entries.cause: `process` is a Node.js global; browsers do not have it, and not every bundler injects it.
entries.denext: denext's client bundles get a small injected `process` shim, so `process.env` reads resolve (to the public env values) instead of throwing.

evidence.name: browserProcessShimPath: an injected process shim serves env reads in a browser bundle

entries.title: "Invalid hook call" from two copies of React
entries.problem: Hooks throw because a library resolved its own copy of React, so the app has two.
errorText: Invalid hook call. Hooks can only be called inside of the body of a function component.

affects.stack: React apps with linked or nested dependencies

entries.cause: A package manager installs a second `react` (a linked package, a mismatched peer range), and each copy keeps its own hook state.
entries.denext: denext maps every React-family specifier (`react`, `react-dom`, `react/jsx-runtime`, …) to its single runtime for the whole module graph, npm libraries included, so there is only one copy.

evidence.name: next-compat REACT_ALIASES covers exactly the full react-family set
resolveReactFamilyFile: mapped specifiers resolve directly

entries.title: Child components re-render when their props did not change
entries.problem: A parent update re-renders every child, so apps wrap components in `memo` or adopt the React Compiler to avoid wasted renders.
entries.cause: React re-renders a component's subtree on every update unless a component is memoized.
entries.denext: denext skips re-rendering a function component whose props are shallow-equal to the last render; context changes still reach consumers. This differs from React, where only `memo` components bail out: code that relied on a child re-rendering with unchanged props should read state or context instead. denext's compiler adds React-Compiler-style memoization without Babel.

evidence.name: auto-bailout: a component with stable props is not re-rendered on a parent update
a compiled parent skips re-rendering a child with stable deps

entries.title: Error boundaries do not catch errors thrown in event handlers
entries.problem: An exception in an `onClick` handler is not caught by the surrounding error boundary, so the UI keeps going in a broken state.
entries.cause: React's error boundaries only catch errors thrown while rendering and in lifecycle methods.
entries.denext: denext routes an error thrown in an event handler to the nearest error boundary, which shows its fallback, as it does for render errors. This differs from React; code that catches its own handler errors is unaffected.

evidence.name: an event-handler error still reaches the boundary after an ancestor re-rendered

entries.title: Icon and utility barrels pulling whole libraries into the bundle
entries.problem: Importing one icon from `lucide-react` (or a function from `date-fns`, `lodash-es`) loads the package's whole barrel file in development and can bloat the bundle.

affects.stack: React apps on Vite or other bundlers

entries.cause: A barrel module re-exports every member, and the bundler has to load it to find the one you used.
entries.denext: Named imports from listed packages are rewritten to the modules that define them, so the barrel is never loaded. A built-in list (lucide-react, date-fns, lodash-es and others) is on by default, in SPA mode too. Next.js offers the same option as `optimizePackageImports`; denext uses the same key.

evidence.name: rewrite: named imports go to their defining modules, aliases kept

entries.title: End-to-end typed API calls without tRPC
entries.problem: Route handlers take and return untyped JSON, so clients either duplicate the types or add tRPC or a code generator.
entries.cause: A `route.ts` handler is a plain `Request` → `Response` function with no schema the client can see.
entries.denext: `defineApi` validates params, query and body with any Standard Schema library (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, …), strips undeclared response keys, and the dev server generates a typed client from the route modules, so `createApiClient()` and `useApi` check every call. GET calls in the same tick share one batched request.

evidence.name: defineApi: parsed params/query/body reach the handler; the return value is JSON
defineApi: the response schema always runs and strips undeclared keys (data-leak guard)
api batch: runs GET/HEAD items through the pipeline and returns each result

entries.title: Live updates and subscriptions without a separate WebSocket server
entries.problem: Pushing live data to the browser from a Next.js app needs a separate WebSocket server or a hosted realtime service.

affects.stack: Next.js route handlers on serverless hosts

entries.cause: Route handlers answer one request with one response; serverless functions do not keep connections open.
entries.denext: denext's server holds the socket: `defineSubscription` validates input, authorizes each subscriber and pushes a new value when a tag is revalidated, and `createChannel` publishes events to authorized subscribers.

evidence.name: defineSubscription hub: validated input, server-derived tags, recompute on invalidation
channel hub: an authorized subscriber receives publishes (codec-encoded), fanned out to every connection

entries.title: Scheduled jobs without a platform cron service
entries.problem: Running a nightly cleanup or digest from a Next.js app needs the host's cron feature, an external scheduler or a queue.
entries.cause: Next.js has no scheduler of its own.
entries.denext: A task in `tasks/<name>.ts` with `defineTask` runs on a cron schedule (`Deno.cron` where available, else a built-in scheduler that never overlaps a running instance), on demand with `runTask()` or `denext task <name>`, with optional run history.

evidence.name: scheduleTasks uses Deno.cron when available and hands it the schedule
userland scheduler: never on registration, once per matching minute, never overlapping, aborted on dispose
a manual CLI run is recorded, exactly like a scheduled one

entries.title: A self-hosted data cache that survives restarts
entries.problem: A self-hosted Next.js app keeps its data and page cache in memory and on the local filesystem; sharing it across instances needs a custom `cacheHandler`.
entries.cause: The default cache handler is local to the process and its disk.
entries.denext: denext's default cache store is a durable `node:sqlite` file (no extra service), and the `CacheStore` interface is pluggable for a shared backend. An unwritable path falls back to memory with one log line, and the health endpoint reports which store is active.

evidence.name: chooseCacheStore: a durable-store path resolves to a functional node:sqlite store
/_denext/health reports the store kind, so a silent fallback to memory is visible from the probe

entries.title: Rate limits bypassed with a forged X-Forwarded-For
entries.problem: A rate limiter keyed on the `x-forwarded-for` header is bypassed by a client that sends a new value with each request.
entries.cause: Any client can set the header; it is only meaningful when a proxy you control overwrites it.
entries.denext: denext's `clientIp()` and its rate limiters use the socket peer address unless you declare a trusted proxy (`trustForwardedHeaders`), and then only the proxy's last hop. The sign-in limiter is on by default.

evidence.name: credentials: a forged x-forwarded-for cannot dodge the limiter (untrusted by default)
rateLimit: the (max+1)th request in a window is a 429 with retry-after; forged XFF is ignored

entries.title: Will my existing app run?
entries.problem: Before trying a new framework, teams want to know whether their existing app runs without a rewrite.
entries.cause: Framework migrations usually start with rewriting imports, config and routes.
entries.denext: `denext migrate` writes config only (a `deno.json` alias map and a `denext.config.ts`), so the app's own source is unchanged for Next.js. Two public apps are migrated, built and rendered by a nightly test: Vercel's App Router playground and the Epic Stack (Remix). `denext migrate --check` reports what would change for your app first.

evidence.name: migration bed: vercel/next-app-router-playground migrates, builds, and renders
migration bed: epicweb-dev/epic-stack (Remix) migrates, builds, and renders

entries.title: Pages Router apps
entries.problem: A `pages/` app uses `getServerSideProps`, `next/router` and `next/head`, which the App Router does not have.
entries.cause: The Pages Router is a separate routing and data model.
entries.denext: `denext migrate` detects `pages/` and wires the `@denext/pages-router` plugin, which runs `getServerSideProps`, `getStaticProps`, `_app`, `_document` and API routes, and points `next/router`, `next/link` and `next/head` at it.

evidence.name: handler runs getServerSideProps and passes props to the page
Pages Router: maps next/router|link|head to the pages-router plugin + pins ^0.8.0

entries.title: next.config wrappers and MDX plugins carried over
entries.problem: A `next.config` wrapped by `createMDX` or a docs framework's plugin hides its options (remark and rehype plugins) inside a webpack loader, so they are lost when moving to another build.
entries.cause: The wrapper stores the plugin functions in a closure that only its webpack loader reads.
entries.denext: `denext migrate` evaluates the config in a sandboxed subprocess (read access to the project only), keeps the honored keys even when a wrapper crashes after returning the config, and the generated config recovers the MDX plugins at build time.

evidence.name: next.config is honored even when a plugin wrapper crashes AFTER exporting it
App Router with MDX plugins: config recovers them at build time (no hand-edit)
resolveNextMdx recovers live remark plugins + providerImportSource from next.config

entries.title: tsconfig path aliases (@/*) in monorepos
entries.problem: `@/*` and other `paths` aliases stop resolving when the build tool does not read the tsconfig, especially when the aliases live in a monorepo-root tsconfig or the file has comments.
entries.cause: `paths` is TypeScript configuration; each bundler reads it differently, and tsconfig files are JSONC.
entries.denext: `denext migrate` reads the tsconfig with a JSONC parser, follows `extends` and a monorepo-root tsconfig, and writes the aliases into the `deno.json` import map relative to the app.

evidence.name: workspace app: monorepo-root tsconfig paths become deno.json aliases (relative to app)
App Router: `@/*` alias survives a tsconfig carrying a `$schema` URL (JSONC parse)

entries.title: React Compiler memoization kept when moving a Vite app
entries.problem: A Vite app that relies on the React Compiler re-renders far more after moving to a build that does not run the Babel plugin.
entries.cause: The compiler's memoization is a build step; without it every component re-renders with its parent.
entries.denext: `denext migrate` detects the React Compiler in the Vite config and turns on denext's own auto-memo compiler (`reactCompiler: true`), which needs no Babel.

evidence.name: migrate SPA: React Compiler in the Vite config enables denext's auto-memo compiler
